head: pr17488-r25
report:
Writing the probe.

## DEFECT: A refused restore leaves a `.restoring` record that stops the live session from opening (P2)

**Mechanism.** `restoreArchivedSessionLocked` (`src/session/session-archive.ts:2260-2262`) creates this run's record with `createRestoreRecord` before it runs any of its refusal checks. The check `Refusing to restore over a different session file` comes later, at line 2275, and nothing is published before it. When it throws, the `finally` (2351-2354) only closes the record's handle. The record stays on disk, holding just the restore command.

That record then does two things:
- **The live session stops opening.** `liveSessionIsComplete` (2398-2401) returns false whenever the record exists, so `materializeSessionFile` sends every later open of the live file into `restoreArchivedSession`. That throws the same "different session file" refusal. This affects `SessionManager` open/resume/fork and render. Before the refused restore, the same session opened normally.
- **The "bring the archived one home" route fails once more.** The refusal says to move the live file aside and run the restore again. On that run `createRestoreRecord` returns `undefined` because the name is taken. At line 2343 the run adds `restoreRecordLeftNote` and exits non-zero, even though everything came home.

The refusal message never mentions the record, and the docstring at 2186 says "A refusal before the copy leaves both trees untouched." Any other throw after line 2262 leaves the same record: an inflate failure, or `noOwners` after `leases.refresh()`.

**Trigger** (probe `refusal-record.test.ts` in my scratch directory):
1. Write a live session and run `gc --archive --apply`; the live copy is kept.
2. Rewrite the live transcript with the same id and a different prompt, so the archive is no longer a prefix of it.
3. Call `materializeSessionFile(live)`, then `restoreArchivedSession(archive)`, then `materializeSessionFile(live)` again.

**Measured:**
```
materialize before restore: ok …/2026-01-01T00-00-00-000Z_<id>.jsonl
record before: false
restore: Refusing to restore over a different session file: …
refusal mentions .restoring: false
record after: true
materialize after restore: threw Refusing to restore over a different session file: …
```

**Fix.** Remove this run's own record (`dropOwnRestoreRecord(own)`) when the restore throws before anything is published. Alternatively, run the different-session refusal before `createRestoreRecord`. Either way the inflate and lease-refresh throws need the same handling.

## DEFECT: CHANGELOG says re-archiving clears the restore record, but the code never removes it (P3)

- CHANGELOG line 18 of the diff says: "Re-archiving clears that record only when every entry the archive holds has a regular file at its live name…".
- CHANGELOG line 35 says: "`gc --archive` never removes it either".
- The code agrees with line 35. `copySessionIntoArchive` (`src/cli/gc-cli.ts:2096-2117`) only reports the record, even when nothing is outstanding ("this run did not write that record, so it was left").

So line 18 is false and contradicts line 35 in the same release notes. Users told that re-archiving clears the record will find the session still treated as unfinished. Fix: change line 18 to match the code.

## NOT A DEFECT

**Earlier round's findings at this head:**
- **astra #1 / claude "forged first line": closed.**
  - The record is now created exclusively (`fs.open(record, "wx")`, 175-192).
  - It is rewritten only through the descriptor that created it.
  - It is removed only if the file renamed aside has the inode taken at creation; anything else is put back with `link`, or left and named (208-231).
  - A regular file already at the name is never read, rewritten or removed, by restore or by archive (`gc-cli.ts:2096-2117`).
  - So the forged-prefix file, the no-newline file and the replace-before-rename race no longer lead to deletion.
- **astra #2 (killed live stage forgotten when the archived artifact directory is absent): closed.**
  - `recordedStagingIn(liveArtifacts)` now runs whether or not `hasArtifacts` is true (2328-2340).
  - A killed restore's own record stays and makes the next restore and its preview report it (preview at `gc-cli.ts:2588-2601`).
- **astra #3 (printed recovery command could stage inside a tree that moved after the check): addressed in the source; I did not re-run it dynamically.**
  - `stagingResidueNote` (1731-1768) now prints real paths.
  - The command re-resolves both session trees with `realpath` when it runs, and stops with `rmdir` if the new directory is inside either tree.
- **claude "read-only archive bucket wording": closed.** `moveAsidePermission` is appended to every refusal about moving the record aside.
- **claude round-21 table (symlink, FIFO, quarantine-symlink, reclaim of non-regular entries, relative `dir`): already closed in that round.** This head's restore record code still refuses any non-regular file at the record's name (114-132).

**Behaviours I examined and left out:**
- **A restore leaves an earlier run's record in place and exits non-zero until someone moves it aside.** The CHANGELOG states this on purpose ("the last step after a restore that did not finish is to look at that record and move it aside"). I only report it where a refusal creates the record itself, above.
- **The full `<timestamp>_<id>` stem in printed commands (`gc-cli.ts:2115`, `2777`, `2796`).** `findArchivedSessionFiles` matches on the whole-name prefix as well as the id, so these commands resolve.

**Test run.** I ran `bun test --timeout 180000 test/session-archive.test.ts test/gc-cli.test.ts` twice: each run had 271 pass, 4 skip and 1 fail. The one failure, `exporting an archived session yields the same document as live`, is environmental. It fails with `Development export viewer not found … Run bun gen:export-viewer`, a generated asset missing from this read-only snapshot.
